prompt: On GKE Autopilot, who chooses the machine type of the nodes?
hint: You describe pods, not machines.

choices.text: Google, from what the pods request
choices.why: Right. There is no node pool to set one on.

choices.text: You, in the cluster's node_config
choices.why: An Autopilot cluster has no node configuration of yours.

choices.text: You, by creating one node pool per machine type
choices.why: Node pools are refused on Autopilot.

choices.text: Nobody: every node is an e2-standard-4
choices.why: Google picks machines to fit the pods; there is no single fixed type.

prompt: Which of these is still your job on Autopilot?
hint: What happens to a one-replica Deployment when its node is replaced?

choices.text: Choosing the surge settings for node upgrades
choices.why: Google upgrades Autopilot nodes; there are no pool settings.

choices.text: Setting the number of nodes in each zone
choices.why: Google adds nodes as pods are scheduled.

choices.text: Replica counts and PodDisruptionBudgets
choices.why: Right. A single replica is still down while its node is replaced.

choices.text: Patching the nodes' operating system
choices.why: Google patches and hardens Autopilot nodes.

prompt: A container on Autopilot requests 2 vCPU and uses a tenth of one. What is it billed for?
hint: On Autopilot the request is the bill.

choices.text: 0.1 vCPU, what it used
choices.why: Autopilot bills requests, not usage.

choices.text: 2 vCPU, every hour it runs
choices.why: Right; on Autopilot the request is the bill.

choices.text: A whole node, since it cannot share one
choices.why: Pods share nodes; you pay for the request.

choices.text: Nothing, until it exceeds its request
choices.why: The request is billed from the moment the pod runs.

prompt: In Terraform, the one line that hands a GKE cluster's nodes over to Google is enable____ = true.
hint: The mode's name, after an underscore.

prompt: What kind of location does an Autopilot cluster always have?
hint: Lesson 13 named both kinds.

choices.text: A single zone, chosen by Google
choices.why: Autopilot clusters are not zonal.

choices.text: Several regions at once
choices.why: A cluster lives in one region.

choices.text: Whatever location the first pod asks for
choices.why: Location is fixed at creation.

choices.text: A region
choices.why: Right; Autopilot clusters are always regional.

prompt: At 0.0445 USD per vCPU-hour and 0.0049225 per GiB-hour, what does one pod requesting 1 vCPU and 4 GiB cost for 730 hours?
hint: vCPU times rate, plus GiB times rate, times 730.

prompt: autopilot.py says two tiny pods cost 19.84 on Autopilot and 97.84 on Standard. Why is Standard so much dearer here?
hint: What is the smallest Standard can be?

choices.text: Standard charges a higher rate per vCPU
choices.why: Per vCPU, the node is cheaper; the waste is the problem.

choices.text: A whole node is paid for, and the pods use a sixteenth of it
choices.why: Right. Autopilot wins when nodes would sit partly empty.

choices.text: Standard adds a cluster fee and Autopilot does not
choices.why: Both pay the fee; the program leaves it out on both sides.

choices.text: Standard nodes reserve half their memory for the system
choices.why: The reservation is 3.92 vCPU and 13.30 GiB left of 4 and 16, far from half.

prompt: The shop's pods cost 212.73 on Autopilot and a 195.67 floor on two Standard nodes. Why does the lesson not call Standard cheaper for the shop?
hint: How many nodes does a regional pool have at least?

choices.text: Autopilot discounts are applied after the month ends
choices.why: No such discount is in the comparison.

choices.text: Standard's price excludes the disks of the nodes
choices.why: True of both sides in a sense, and not the reason given.

choices.text: A regional pool needs a node in each zone: three, at 293.51
choices.why: Right. The 195.67 assumed two nodes in one zone, packed perfectly.

choices.text: autopilot.py rounds Standard down to whole nodes
choices.why: It rounds up, not down.

prompt: Which of these does autopilot.py leave out? Choose all that apply.
hint: The program says what it does not model.

choices.text: The system pods GKE runs on each Standard node
choices.why: Right; they make the real room smaller.

choices.text: Autopilot raising requests below its minimums
choices.why: Right; the raised values are billed.

choices.text: The memory GKE reserves on a Standard node
choices.why: allocatable() models exactly that.

choices.text: The rate per GiB-hour of Autopilot memory
choices.why: POD_GIB is in the program.

prompt: Order these by monthly cost, cheapest first, from the lesson's runs of autopilot.py.
items: The shop's eight pods on Standard
trap: Standard is not always the dear one: it is the cheapest per vCPU once pods fill its nodes.

prompt: terraform plan accepted a google_container_node_pool on an Autopilot cluster. What would happen on apply?
hint: Can the pool alone tell what kind of cluster it joins?

choices.text: The pool would be created and ignored by the scheduler
choices.why: Autopilot does not accept node pools at all.

choices.text: The cluster would switch to Standard to hold it
choices.why: A cluster's mode never changes after creation.

choices.text: Terraform would ask whether to convert the cluster
choices.why: Terraform has no such prompt; there is nothing to convert to.

choices.text: GKE would refuse it, after the cluster existed
choices.why: Right. The rule crosses two resources, so the plan cannot see it.

prompt: Which of these does Autopilot refuse?
hint: Anything that depends on the node being yours.

choices.text: A Deployment with three replicas
choices.why: Ordinary workloads run unchanged.

choices.text: A pod that asks for a GPU
choices.why: Autopilot picks a node with a GPU for it.

choices.text: A privileged container
choices.why: Right; it is refused when the pod is created.

choices.text: A DaemonSet for a monitoring agent
choices.why: Allowed, and billed on every node it lands on.

prompt: A pod asks for interruptible, cheaper capacity with the node selector cloud.google.com/gke-___: "true".
hint: The pricing model's own name, in lower case.

prompt: A team adds remove_default_node_pool = true to its Autopilot cluster and validate refuses at once, while a separate node pool resource passed. What explains the difference?
hint: Where does each rule live?

choices.text: The first conflict is inside one resource; the second crosses two
choices.why: Right. The provider checks what one resource says about itself.

choices.text: validate runs stricter checks than plan does
choices.why: plan runs the same checks and more.

choices.text: The node pool resource is not supported by provider 8.9.0
choices.why: It is, and lesson 13 planned one.

choices.text: remove_default_node_pool is deprecated everywhere
choices.why: The error is a conflict with enable_autopilot, not a deprecation.

prompt: Match each need to how a pod gets it on Autopilot.
hint: You choose hardware through the pod.

pairs.right: Ask for it in the pod's resources

pairs.left: A different balance of processor and price

pairs.right: Not available; use kubectl and logs

right_distractors: A node pool with a taint

prompt: Can an existing Standard cluster be converted to Autopilot?
hint: The mode is set once.

choices.text: Yes, by setting enable_autopilot = true and applying
choices.why: The mode is fixed at creation; changing it means a new cluster.

choices.text: Yes, once every node pool has been deleted
choices.why: Deleting pools does not change the mode.

choices.text: No: build a new one of that kind and redeploy
choices.why: Right. The Kubernetes objects mostly move unchanged.

choices.text: Only on the EXTENDED release channel
choices.why: Channels decide versions, not modes.

prompt: Which question comes first when choosing between Standard and Autopilot?
hint: One answer makes the price irrelevant.

choices.text: How full would Standard's nodes be?
choices.why: Second: it matters only if Autopilot can run everything.

choices.text: Is the load uneven through the day?
choices.why: Third, and again a price question.

choices.text: Who would look after the nodes?
choices.why: Fourth, and weighed against price.

choices.text: Does anything need what Autopilot refuses?
choices.why: Right. If yes, that workload needs Standard whatever the price.

prompt: A team of two runs a few small services that are busy by day and idle at night, and one log agent that needs a host path. What is the cheapest sound plan?
hint: Is the agent needed at all?

choices.text: A Standard cluster sized for the daytime peak
choices.why: It pays for empty nodes every night.

choices.text: One Autopilot and one Standard cluster for the agent
choices.why: A second cluster fee and pool for an agent the platform replaces.

choices.text: Autopilot, with the platform's own logging instead of the agent
choices.why: Right. GKE ships logs to Cloud Logging already, so the refused workload disappears.

choices.text: Autopilot, with the agent run as a privileged DaemonSet
choices.why: Privileged pods are refused on Autopilot.

prompt: Autopilot wins when Standard's nodes would sit partly ___.
hint: The opposite of full.

prompt: Autopilot Spot pods list at 0.0133 USD per vCPU-hour against 0.0445 on demand. What share of the on-demand vCPU price is saved, in percent, rounded to a whole number?
hint: One minus the ratio.

prompt: Twelve pods of 1 vCPU and 4 GiB cost 391.35 on Standard and 562.30 on Autopilot. Which statement fits?
hint: How full are the four nodes?

choices.text: Autopilot is always dearer for more than ten pods
choices.why: The count does not decide; how full nodes are does.

choices.text: Steady pods fill the nodes, and a node is cheaper per vCPU
choices.why: Right; that is when Standard wins.

choices.text: Standard here leaves out the cluster fee, and Autopilot does not
choices.why: Both leave it out.

choices.text: Autopilot bills the memory twice, once per zone
choices.why: Requests are billed once.

prompt: Put the four questions for choosing a mode in the lesson's order.
hint: A refusal outranks a price.
items: Does anything need what Autopilot refuses?
How full would Standard's nodes be?
Who would look after the nodes?

prompt: On Autopilot, what decides when a pod's node is replaced for an upgrade?
hint: You have one lever left.

choices.text: The pod's own upgrade_settings
choices.why: Pods have no upgrade settings.

choices.text: A node pool's max_surge
choices.why: There is no node pool on Autopilot.

choices.text: Nothing: Autopilot nodes are never replaced
choices.why: They are replaced; you just do not control how.

choices.text: Google, inside the cluster's maintenance window
choices.why: Right. The window is the lever you keep.

prompt: Which of these are billed on Autopilot? Choose all that apply.
hint: Requests, while they run, and one flat fee.

choices.text: The cluster management fee
choices.why: Right; Autopilot pays it like Standard.

choices.text: Each DaemonSet pod on every node it lands on
choices.why: Right; a DaemonSet multiplies with the nodes.

choices.text: The empty space on the nodes Google runs
choices.why: That is exactly what Autopilot does not bill.

choices.text: A pod's requests while it is not running
choices.why: Requests are billed while pods run.
